title: What to eat
intro:
One splurge, everything else low-friction. The anchor is Saturday dinner — everything else here is walk-in or a one-tap online booking, never a project.

Both markets follow the Tokyo Central Wholesale Market calendar, so Sunday is the wrong morning for either one: Saturday is the Tsukiji morning, Monday the Toyosu one. The trap worth naming up front is inside Toyosu — Sushi Dai and Daiwa Sushi run 2–5 hour waits and will likely split a party of six into two seatings. Browse the market instead.

items.name: Nihonryori RyuGin
items.how: Overseas guests book through a Tokyo hotel concierge or an approved partner (e.g. My Concierge Japan) — no direct self-service reservation. Bookings open on the 1st of the month for the months ahead, so October dates open Sept 1, 2026; have your concierge call at opening. ⚠ RyuGin will not accept a reservation from a guest who declares a food allergy, and cannot serve anyone who doesn't eat fish or seafood. Children must be 10 or older, and eight is the maximum party.
items.crowd_tip: Private Room 1 (6–8 seats) or Private Room 2 (5–8 seats) fit a party of six without splitting the group; the private-room service charge is 15% rather than the 10% charged at table seats.
items.why: 3 Michelin stars — the trip's anchor dinner, and the only finalist confirmed to seat six in one room.

items.name: Ginza Ukai-tei
items.closed: Sundays, twice a month on Mondays
items.how: Genuine self-service English-language online booking — no concierge needed. The booking form takes up to 6 adults; seven or more has to go by phone.
items.crowd_tip: Private rooms are prepared for parties over four, and a chef cooks the teppanyaki course in front of you rather than sending it out from a kitchen.
items.why: The anchor's low-friction fallback if RyuGin's Sept 1 booking window closes first — still Michelin-starred teppanyaki, bookable for six in two taps.

items.name: Aragawa
items.how: TableCheck online, 1–10 guests, credit card required to hold the reservation. The October Tajima-beef seasonal course is listed tax-included with the 12% service charge added on top.
items.crowd_tip: ⚠ Total restaurant capacity is reported at only ≈22 seats (a press estimate, not an official figure) — a table for six is a large fraction of the room on a Saturday. Book as early as possible if attempting this instead of RyuGin.
items.why: Worth the Effort: independent critics rank it among the best steak experiences in Japan — a genuinely different, splurge-tier alternative if you'd rather have this than the anchor dinner.

items.name: Kobikicho Ohno
items.address: 東京都新宿区四谷3-6 — 1 min from Yotsuya-sanchome Station (Marunouchi Line)
items.hours: Dinner 17:00–21:00 (drinks last order 20:00); no fixed weekly closure day, irregular ad-hoc closures — confirm for your exact date
items.how: Serves only ONE party per day — the whole restaurant is a single nightly seating, so there's no release-window date to wait for; contact as early as practical for Sat Oct 17 since another party could take the date first. ⚠ No fixed course price is published anywhere on the restaurant's own site; ask for the evening's price when you book. Card acceptance isn't published either. English menu and English-speaking staff are listed.
items.crowd_tip: Six seats total, all in one horigotatsu private room (door and walls) for 2–6 — a party of six fills the restaurant exactly, with zero buffer for a seventh guest.
items.why: Worth the Effort: a tea-kaiseki restaurant discoverable only through Japanese-language search, serving a single reservation a day — a genuinely exclusive alternative to RyuGin if the concierge booking doesn't come through, at real booking-friction cost (no self-service, no published price, capacity fits 6 with no margin).

items.name: Yakiniku Ushigoro
items.how: Self-service TableCheck booking, no concierge needed. Courses are listed tax-included with a 10% service charge added.
items.crowd_tip: Online booking takes parties of 2–6, so six is the largest table you can reserve without phoning — seven or more needs a call.
items.why: A lower-key wagyu yakiniku night — the trip's second real dinner, without RyuGin-level booking friction.

items.name: Uobei Genki Sushi
items.address: 東京都渋谷区道玄坂2-29-11 第六セントラルビル1階
items.how: Tablet ordering, bullet-train plate delivery — no reservations taken at all. 90 seats, all counter, so six of you sit in a row rather than around a table. ⚠ Cash only: no cards and no QR payments.
items.why: The easiest possible group dinner for a jet-lagged arrival night — no booking, no wait to speak of.

items.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
items.hours: Best 6:30–9 AM; shops run on the Tokyo Central Wholesale Market business-day calendar, so Sundays and some Wednesdays are reduced — Saturday is the trip's market morning here
items.how: Graze stall to stall rather than one sit-down meal — the market's own site asks visitors not to move through the narrow lanes in large groups, so split into pairs or trios while browsing.
items.crowd_tip: 10 AM–1 PM is the most crowded window, with lines at the famous stalls; go earlier.
items.why: The wholesale tuna auction moved to Toyosu in 2018, but the food stalls here never closed — still the best casual grazing breakfast in the city.

items.name: Toyosu Market
items.closed: Sundays, public holidays, and scheduled market closure days (usually Wednesdays)
items.hours: Public hours 5:00–17:00 on operating days; individual shops keep their own
items.how: ⚠ No Wednesday falls in this trip and Mon Oct 19 is a normal business day, but the market publishes its 2026 closure grid as a downloadable calendar rather than a page — confirm October before you go.
items.crowd_tip: Skip Sushi Dai/Daiwa Sushi's counters — 2–5 hour waits, and a party of six will likely be split into two seatings. Browse the market itself instead and save the splurge sushi for Saturday.
items.why: Where the wholesale fish trade actually is now — pairs naturally with teamLab Planets, a few minutes away.

items.name: Torien
items.hours: Mon–Thu/Sun/holidays 11:30–23:30, Fri–Sat 11:30–23:45; food and drink last order 23:00; closed only New Year's Day
items.how: 150 seats, with 3F private rooms for 20–30 and whole-floor rentals on request — one of the few Omoide Yokocho places that seats a group at all, rather than the small counters the alley is built from.
items.why: The practical way to eat together at Omoide Yokocho as one group of six instead of splitting across several tiny stalls.

items.name: Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko)
items.how: ≈400 shops/stalls over 500m — pure grazing, zero reservation friction.
items.crowd_tip: Weekday mornings, especially before lunch, are calmest; weekends and the pre-New Year season get significantly more crowded.
items.why: A real working shopping street, not a themed tourist arcade — a relaxed last-morning food crawl before the airport.
